name: Freelance marketplaces
one_line: Matches businesses with independent freelancers for project work, and takes a cut of what the client pays.
sells: A place for businesses to find, hire and pay independent freelancers for project work, in exchange for a fee on the money that changes hands
customers: Businesses and individuals hiring freelance talent, and the freelancers who sell their skills by the project
suppliers: Cloud hosting, payment processors (to move money between client and freelancer, with escrow), and the freelancers who supply the labor

revenue.metric: estimated revenue of the leading freelance / online-staffing marketplaces
revenue.period: FY2025 for the public leaders; estimates for the private tail
revenue.basis: industry (SEC filings for Upwork and Fiverr; estimates for the rest)
revenue.note: Upwork ($787.8M) and Fiverr ($430.9M) FY2025 are hard numbers and make up most of the total; Toptal, Freelancer.com, Guru, Malt and PeoplePerHour add the rest (estimated). The money freelancers actually earn through these platforms is far larger than the fee business: Upwork's gross services volume alone is ~$4.0B/yr, so total freelancer earnings across the sector run to several billion dollars a year.

structure.why: Two generalist platforms lead the open Western market — Upwork (~half the sector's revenue) and Fiverr (~a quarter) — above a vetted-premium tier (Toptal) and a long tail of regional and niche marketplaces.
structure.hhi_note: Shares given only to the two public leaders (Upwork ~49%, Fiverr ~27% of the ~$1.6B set), so a concentrated, Upwork-led market; squared-share HHI of those two alone is ~3,150 (a lower bound).

econ: A two-sided marketplace that matches clients with freelancers and takes a cut of each project. Its value is trust and plumbing — vetting, ratings, escrow and payments — because strangers will not otherwise exchange work and money online. The built-in tension is disintermediation: once a client and freelancer have met, both are tempted to take the relationship off-platform to dodge the fee, so marketplaces defend their take rate with reputation systems, escrow and payment lock-in. Fiverr charges a high ~28% take on productized 'gigs'; Upwork runs an open hourly marketplace plus enterprise; Toptal vets hard and charges a premium.

companies.name: Upwork
companies.share_basis: share of estimated leading-marketplace revenue (~$1.6B set), FY2025 revenue basis
companies.note: Largest open marketplace; $4.03B GSV, 785K active clients; Marketplace $682.9M + Enterprise $104.9M.

companies.name: Fiverr
companies.share_basis: share of estimated leading-marketplace revenue (~$1.6B set), FY2025 revenue basis
companies.note: Productized 'gig' marketplace; marketplace take rate 27.7%; 3.1M active buyers; Services revenue up ~51%.

companies.name: Toptal
companies.note: Bootstrapped, vetted 'top 3%' network for developers, designers and finance talent; premium rates, no public revenue figure.

companies.name: Freelancer.com
companies.note: Public (ASX: FLN); contest-and-bid marketplace plus Escrow.com; smaller than the leaders.

companies.name: Malt
companies.note: Europe's largest freelance marketplace; direct freelancer–client matching with managed services, strong in France, Germany and Spain.

products_note: Flagship products as of Nov 2026, checked against each platform's site and FY2025 filings. Shares are given only to the two public leaders (Upwork, Fiverr), whose FY2025 revenue is filed; private platforms don't publish comparable revenue, so their shares are null and the map draws them beside an 'All others' block. Toptal's revenue is a third-party estimate.
